resources.string: Tap Fetch to read the eSIM EID from the device. If Android blocks it, Fetch uses managed config qa_device_eid when your EMM provides one.
EID requires Android 9 (API 28) or a device with eUICC / telephony
No EID from device or managed configuration
eUICC service reports disabled on this device
Device APIs blocked EID. Set managed config qa_device_eid from your EMM (AMAPI hardwareInfo.euiccChipInfo), then tap Fetch again.
Phone permission denied — cannot read EID. Tap Fetch again and allow Phone, or enable it in App info → Permissions.
Could not read EID — see details above
Optional. EMM can set this to the eUICC EID (e.g. from Android Management API hardwareInfo.euiccChipInfo). Used when on-device getEid() is blocked for third-party apps.
No app can handle this action.
If your MDM shows a policy but this screen stays empty, confirm the catalog / app record uses this exact application ID (not the Java package path):\n%1$s
Optional text shown at the top of the QA screen.

URL for the Open test URL action. Leave empty to use the APK Forge endpoint from the build (gradle.properties app.apk_forge_endpoint). You may also set this to the sentinel APK_Forge to use that same endpoint explicitly.
Optional line appended to the build information block (for QA labels / ticket IDs).
Seconds (integer in schema; some EMMs still send a string — the app parses both). Suggested range 5–300 for demos.
Single-select value (stored as a string: prod, staging, or dev).
Multi-select checklist (stored as selected entryValues in the restrictions bundle).
Hides/disables the Print action for policy testing.
Disables the Save to files (SAF) action.
Disables the Open test URL action.
Disables the Email build info action.
Disables the Copy for ticket action.
